evidence: paper: Y = v_r r^{d_r} + v_t t \pmod{\mathbb{Z}^2}.

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The formula is the second component of GraphCalculus.graph: q.1^d • vr + q.2 • vt with q = (r,t), which is v_r r^{d_r} + v_t t term for term (the Lean keeps (r,t) alongside in a `Lift` pair so that the chain rule of (6.4) can be stated). Two encoding choices. (i) The "mod ℤ²" is not in the type: Y is valued in ℝ² (the universal cover), and the quotient is carried separately by SlotGeometry.torusEq (x ≡ y iff x − y ∈ ℤ²) and by modelling functions on 𝕋² as ℤ²-indexed Fourier series on ℝ² (TorusInverse module doc: "We work on the universal cover ℝ × ℝ, with frequencies in ℤ × ℤ"); since ℝ² → 𝕋² is a group quotient, the cover representative plus torusEq is the same object. (ii) GraphCalculus.graph is stated for arbitrary d, vr, vt; the specialization to the (6.2) data is PhysicalGraphBounds.nativeGraph, where r^{d_r} appears as radiusPower d y = (y₁²+y₂²)^{d/2} on the two Cartesian radial coordinates. In GraphCalculus the power q.1 ^ d is Real.rpow, so the formula is used away from r = 0 (the module doc says the radial formulas are stated away from r = 0), matching the paper's use on an annulus.
